# dsh-site-bridge
**English** · Русский · 中文

**Hands and eyes for DeepSeek Harness in your own browser.**
Capture a page's markup and its BFF tra

ffic into files an agent can read, drive the page with trusted
input, and verify the extension you j
ust wrote — live, in the same tab.
Two halves, one bridge:
| Half | What it does |
| **DSH plugin** (`lib/`) | Owns the loopback bridge and exposes eleven tools to the model. Writes t

he snapshot bundle into the session workspace. |
| **MV3 extension** (`extension/`) | Lives in your
Chrome/Edge profile, works with your cookies, captures markup and network over CDP, drives the page
with real input events. Localized: English, Русский, 中文. |
Neither half is useful alone: the plugin holds the model-facing surface and the files, the extension
holds the browser session and the fidelity.
## Why
Writing an extension that embeds into someone else's site is mostly archaeology: what the markup is
actually made of, which selector survives the next deploy, and which BFF endpoint this button calls
with which payload. By hand that means DevTools, copy-paste and guesses.
This project turns the archaeology into a capture:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The agent reads those files like any other source and writes the extension. Then `site_inject` runs
that code in the live page, so "it should work" becomes "it works here".
## Features

- **Markup** — element tree with boxes and visibility, computed styles of interactive nodes, CSS
var

iables of the theme, and selector candidates ranked by stability (`data-testid` > `id` > `name` >
`a

ria-label` > class path > positional path), each checked for uniqueness against the live DOM.
- **BF

F traffic** — `xhr`/`fetch` with method, status, request headers, request body, response
headers and

response body, scoped to the inspected site.
- **Trusted input** — clicks, typing, select, key pres

ses, scrolling and file uploads through CDP
`Input.*` / `DOM.setFileInputFiles`: events the page can

not tell apart from a human's.
- **Virtual cursor** — a DOM overlay that moves to the target plus a

real mouse event at those
coordinates, for controls that ignore synthetic `click()`.
- **Deep select

ors** — `host >>> inner` resolves through open shadow roots and same-origin iframes;
click coordinat

es are corrected for frame offsets.
- **Works in background tabs** — reading, clicking, typing and s

creenshots work while the tab is not
focused (Chrome throttles only timers and animation there).
- *
*No stored credentials** — see Security.
### How this differs from browser automation plugins
There are plugins that hand an agent `browser_*` tools: navigate, click, type, read the page. This i

s
not one of them, even though it can do those things — input here is the instrument that verifies a
capture, not the product.

The product is the capture: the DOM with boxes and computed styles, theme CSS variables, selector
ca

ndidates checked for uniqueness, and the site's own xhr/fetch calls with headers and bodies, all
wri
tten to files an agent can read. Automation exists so that "this selector works" and "this BFF call
passes with my cookies" are checked against the live page instead of assumed.
The practical consequence: this plugin is built for writing an extension for one specific site, and
the input tools exist to verify that work against the live page rather than to browse the web.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the `dsh` CLI and a profile (Desktop or Web).
- Chrome or Edge 125+ (the ext

ension uses `chrome.debugger` and MV3 service workers).
- Node.js 22+ for the tooling in `tools/` an

ome.debugger` and MV3 service workers).
- Node.js 22+ for the tooling in `tools/` and for the tests.
## Install
### 1. Host half
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That pulls the published package. From a local checkout instead:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The script links the plugin into your profile, adds it to `dsh.profile.bundles`, and stages the
exte
nsion into `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\site-bridge\extension`. Manual equivalent:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Add `"dsh-site-bridge"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\package.jso

n`
if the CLI did not, then restart DSH — the host half loads at profile start.
## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The wire protocol is small and documented in docs/protocol.md.
## Security

- **Credentials never leave the browser.** The extension does not read cookies or tokens: the page
m

akes its own requests and the browser attaches them. The bridge sees them in flight, but values of
`

cookie`, `authorization`, `x-csrf-token`, `x-api-key`, `set-cookie` and similar headers,
credential-

shaped query parameters and credential-shaped JSON/form fields are replaced with
`«redacted»` **on i

ngest** — before anything is stored.
- **Nothing credential-shaped is written to disk.** Header *nam

es* are kept, because "this endpoint
needs `x-csrf-token`" is part of the contract; the value is not

.
- **Capture is site-scoped.** Only the inspected site's own `xhr`/`fetch` (same host, same
registr

able domain, or third-party JSON) is recorded. Telemetry and security agents that POST a full
page d

ump to their servers are filtered out — otherwise page source with inline tokens would land in
the b

undle.
- **Loopback only.** The bridge binds `127.0.0.1` and rejects any request without the 32-byte

pairing
token. `site_status` prints the path to the token file, not the token.
- **Residual risk.**

Header values and bodies still pass through the DSH process in memory. If a site
puts a secret unde

r an unusual key, redaction will not recognise it. Treat a capture bundle as
sensitive, exactly like

redaction will not recognise it. Treat a capture bundle as
sensitive, exactly like any traffic dump.
## Limitations

Cross-origin iframes, closed shadow roots and body size caps are analysed in
docs/limitations.md — w

ith the exact code location, the plan to remove each and
the expected cost.
